cards.question: What is wkayaobama-skills, and what kinds of content does it hold?
cards.answer: A personal library of Claude Code commands and skills: salvation plans, ETL method, PDF salvage, a rigor hook.
cards.explanation: A command is what you ask Claude to read; skills are pulled in on demand (see 40). Only the PDF salvage skill ships Node and Python scripts; the rigor skill ships one PowerShell hook; the rest is methodology text.
cards.anchor: A toolbox that travels in the car boot: at each garage you open only the drawer the job needs and never tip the whole box out.
cards.evidence_quote: Personal skills and commands for Claude Code.

cards.question: Which single environment variable makes wkayaobama-skills portable from one machine to the next?
cards.answer: `CLAUDE__ROOT` (TWO underscores): set once per machine; every skill and command path starts from it.
cards.explanation: The maintenance rules forbid relative paths in skill files. Breaks if unset: every `${CLAUDE__ROOT}/...` reference inside a command resolves to nothing.
cards.evidence_quote: All skill files use `${CLAUDE__ROOT}` as the absolute root. Set once per machine.

cards.question: Which file holds everything corpus-specific in wkayaobama-skills' PDF salvage, so `build.js` never changes per document family?
cards.answer: `config.json`, one per corpus: labels, regex, thresholds, style, badge highlights, meta.
cards.explanation: A wrong classification is fixed by adding a label or a regex there, never by editing `build.js`. Not fully true yet: `preview.js` still hard-codes one corpus's page title.
cards.example: node build.js raw.json config.json output.docx  # same script, another corpus = another config
cards.confusables: `raw.json` — it is the stage-1 DUMP of text items and path boxes produced by `parse.js`; `config.json` is AUTHORED by hand per corpus.
cards.evidence_quote: **Don't make `build.js` smarter to fit one corpus.** Add a regex or label to that corpus's `config.json` instead. The script should stay corpus-agnostic.

cards.question: wkayaobama-skills · pipeline-salvation: complete the four buckets into which a salvation plan classifies every file.
cards.explanation: KEEP powers the runnable core; REWRITE-MINIMAL is boundary cleanup only (say WHAT changes, not 'refactor'); DEFER is useful later; DROP is noise. Every file of the main package goes into exactly one.
cards.confusables: cf. [private project] skills/pipeline-salvation: the GENERIC variant of the same four buckets; the copy here adds separate tables per system (Python layer and Workflowps).
cards.evidence_quote: 3. **Four Buckets** — Keep / Rewrite-minimal / Defer / Drop (separate tables per system)

cards.question: wkayaobama-skills · salvage-pdf-to-word: recite the 5 script runs from the source PDF to `preview.html`.
steps: `render_canvas.py <pdf> <out_png>` -> PNG of the first page, 50 DPI by default
`slice_canvas.py <in_png> <out_dir>` -> 6 horizontal bands by default: the ground truth
cards.explanation: Stage 2 is two scripts (render, then slice). You then iterate build -> preview on `config.json` until the preview matches the slices; `output.ir.json` tells a classification error from an emission error. Stage 1 carries a latent, unconfirmed crash: see 91.
cards.anchor: A tailor unpicks a coat into numbered pieces, pins a photo of it on the wall in strips, sews a new coat from the pieces, then tries it on facing the photo.
cards.evidence_quote: PDF ─► (1) parse.js ─► raw.json (text items + rect ops, top-left coords) (2) render_canvas.py + slice_canvas.py ─► PNG bands for visual reference (3) build.js + config.json ─► output.docx + output.ir.json (IR for review)

cards.question: At which level of wkayaobama-skills' probe ladder does a live production write happen, and what does it require?
cards.answer: Level 5, the LAST: explicit human approval, no exceptions; levels are never skipped.
cards.explanation: Ascending risk: 1 local contract tests, 2 dry run or server start, 3 read-only live probe, 4 full staging run, 5 approved live. `execute_plan` runs levels 1 to 4 itself and stops before 5.
cards.confusables: cf. [private project] skills/pipeline-salvation Probe Discipline: also five steps ending in an approved live run, but its step 2 is GENERATED ARTIFACTS; here level 2 is a DRY RUN or server start.
cards.evidence_quote: | 5 | Approved live | Requires explicit human approval. No exceptions. |

cards.question: Which command file of wkayaobama-skills do you ask Claude to read and follow first, before touching code on a multi-step task?
cards.answer: `commands/write_plan.md`: it writes a salvation plan and saves it under `~/.claude/plans/`.
cards.explanation: Trap: its Step 0 reads `${CLAUDE__ROOT}/dashboard/...` and `${CLAUDE__ROOT}/Workflowps/...`; neither directory exists in this repository, so that step only resolves inside the source project's layout.
cards.confusables: `commands/execute_plan.md` — it EXECUTES an existing plan checkpoint by checkpoint; `write_plan.md` only WRITES the plan and touches no code.
cards.evidence_quote: | `commands/write_plan.md` | Before touching code on a multi-step task |

cards.question: wkayaobama-skills · `classifyLine` in `build.js`: predict the `kind` returned by the call below.
cards.answer: `banner-heading` — the font-size test runs BEFORE every regex, so a big line is a banner even when its text matches `formHeading`.
cards.explanation: (1) `t` is non-empty, so not `empty`. (2) 32 >= 30, so the function returns at once. (3) The `formHeading` test below is never reached. At font size 11 the same text would be `form-heading`.
cards.confusables: `form-heading` — decided by the `formHeading` REGEX on the text; `banner-heading` is decided by FONT SIZE alone and is tested first.

cards.question: wkayaobama-skills: a command (`commands/*.md`) vs a skill (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`): what is the ONE difference?
cards.answer: A command is what you ASK Claude to read and follow; a skill is a methodology reference that the command PULLS IN by its `${CLAUDE__ROOT}` path when needed.
cards.explanation: Hence the rule not to load all skills into every session. Breaks if undone: every session carries the whole library as context.
cards.anchor: You hand the cook one recipe card; the card itself sends him to fetch only the jars it names from the shelf.
cards.confusables: skill (`SKILL.md`) — it is REFERENCED from inside a command; a command is INVOKED directly by the owner.
cards.evidence_quote: **Do not load all skills into every session.** Each skill is referenced from within a command when needed.

cards.question: Which Claude Code hook event runs wkayaobama-skills' `rigor-reminder.ps1`?
cards.answer: `UserPromptSubmit`: the seven-point checklist is injected BEFORE the assistant answers.
cards.explanation: The settings entry attaches a `matcher` regex of decision words (recommend, compare, vs, design ...) and a 5-second timeout; per the skill, only matching prompts get the checklist.
cards.confusables: `PreToolUse` (Option 2, not enabled) — it BLOCKS tool calls until sequential thinking has run; `UserPromptSubmit` only INJECTS a reminder.

cards.question: Why does wkayaobama-skills enforce the rigor checklist with a harness hook rather than a memory or `CLAUDE.md` rule?
cards.answer: The memory rule already existed and the assistant still skipped it; a hook injects the checklist MECHANICALLY, whatever the assistant chooses to recall.
cards.explanation: Breaks if undone: back to the cycle where the owner pushes back, the assistant acknowledges the rule, and skips it again next session. The hook enforces the PROCESS only; the assistant may still ignore the injected text (see 99).
cards.anchor: A note pinned in the corridor that everyone walks past, replaced by a doorman who puts the note in your hand each time you come in.
cards.confusables: memory / `CLAUDE.md` rule — it depends on the assistant CHOOSING to apply it; the hook fires in the harness regardless.
cards.evidence_quote: Memory-only enforcement is insufficient — the rule existed in the project's `feedback_research_rigor.md` and the assistant still skipped it. The harness must enforce it mechanically.

cards.question: Why does wkayaobama-skills' salvage-pdf-to-word rebuild structure from positions and vector operators rather than trust the PDF's tags, as `pdf2docx` does?
cards.answer: In forms and flat PDFs the structure is VISUAL only (position, font size, proximity); a tag-trusting converter returns flat paragraphs in scan order.
cards.explanation: `pdfjs-dist` exposes both `getTextContent()` and `getOperatorList()`, enough to rebuild lines and blocks. Breaks if undone: two-column form rows and checkbox lists are flattened. For a clean, tagged PDF the cheap converter is still tried first.
cards.anchor: A form shredded on the floor: you ignore the label on its folder and rebuild the page from where each scrap landed and how big its letters are.
cards.confusables: `pdf2docx` / Acrobat export — they ASSUME the PDF carries tagged structure; the salvage scripts IGNORE tags.
cards.evidence_quote: Salvage flips the strategy: ignore tags, rebuild structure from positions.

cards.question: After installing wkayaobama-skills' rigor hook, how do you check that it fires, and what is the passing sign?
cards.answer: Restart Claude Code and send a prompt containing a trigger word such as "recommend"; the status line briefly shows `Injecting rigor discipline reminder...`.
cards.explanation: Hooks are loaded at startup, hence the restart. No automated test is committed; for the PDF scripts the check is visual: the preview against the slices.
cards.confusables: cf. [private project] claude/settings.json: the INSTALLED hook entry with the same matcher; this repository holds only the SNIPPET to merge.

cards.question: wkayaobama-skills · stage 1 of the PDF salvage stops with `ReferenceError: pendingRects is not defined`. Which statement raised it, and what is the fix?
cards.answer: `pendingRects = [];` in the `OPS.endPath` case of `parse()` in `parse.js` — the declared variable is `pendingPaths`; an ES module is strict, so assigning an undeclared name THROWS. Fix: `pendingPaths = [];`.
cards.explanation: Derived by reading, not by running: `scripts/package.json` sets `"type": "module"`, and the only declaration is `let pendingPaths = [];`. It fires the first time a no-paint (clipping) path reaches `endPath`.

cards.question: wkayaobama-skills' salvage-pdf-to-word SKILL.md accepts single- or multi-page PDFs; how many pages does `parse.js` actually read?
cards.answer: ONE: `pdf.getPage(1)`. Later pages are silently ignored, and `render_canvas.py` likewise renders only `pdf[0]`.
cards.explanation: The scripts were written for one very tall canvas page (`slice_canvas.py` even uncaps Pillow's pixel limit), which hides the gap. Fix: loop over pages with a per-page y offset.

cards.question: wkayaobama-skills: the soft rigor reminder (Option 1) keeps being ignored and you decide to escalate to the blocking `PreToolUse` hook (Option 2). What do you verify first, what is the risk, and how do you roll back?
cards.answer: Verify the hook's stdin JSON BEFORE enforcing. (1) The blocking script ASSUMES fields `tool_name` and `tool_use_history`; first run the diagnostic variant that only logs the JSON. (2) Risk: if the allowlist check fails, the sequential-thinking call itself is blocked, a deadlock. (3) Rollback: remove the `PreToolUse` and `Stop` blocks from `~/.claude/settings.json`; Option 1 keeps firing.
cards.explanation: This is the documented next step of the rigor gate: Option 2 costs three scripts, three settings entries and a marker-file lifecycle, so it stays deferred until Option 1 is shown to be insufficient. See 60.
cards.confusables: Option 1 (`UserPromptSubmit` reminder) — SOFT: the reminder is injected and may be ignored; Option 2 is HARD: the tool call is blocked.
cards.evidence_quote: The exact shape of the JSON delivered to PreToolUse hooks via stdin should be verified against the Claude Code hook documentation before enabling.
